subject: Myth & Symbolism
subcategory: The World Tree and Cosmic Maps
title: What Is the Axis Mundi
description: A micro-lesson that makes What Is the Axis Mundi usable.

hook.text: Every ancient culture placed something at the center of the world—a tree, a pillar, or a mountain. A cosmic spine.

buildup.text: The axis mundi connects heaven, earth, and underworld. It's the vertical line around which the entire cosmos rotates.

discovery.text: Mircea Eliade named this concept: the sacred center where all realms touch. Every temple tried to recreate it.

twist.text: The axis mundi means every sacred place claims to be the center of the world. Jerusalem, Mecca, Delphi—all centers.

climax.text: The need for a center is psychological as much as cosmological. Humans need to feel the world has a midpoint.

punchline.text: Every culture stands at the center. All of them.

quiz.question: What does the axis mundi connect in world mythology?
